items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: This Johnny Dunn, later on, worked with Mamie Smith and I guess Bessie Smith and Clara Smith and everybody else.

ctx.x: Well, I wasn't trying for a sound, I was trying to eat, as I said before. You see, so it worked out. And from then on, now we're starting to have, people are starting to come in and wouldn't do very little dancing. We had to resort to such things like the blues and some of the little pop numbers in order to get them to dance. Because they were so sitting listening (unintelligible), and I had tried something new. I had tried using augmented chords, which gave it a sort of foreign effect. And at that time in wa-wa…

the one thing quiet as it's kept. That's the one thing that made Duke Ellington. The wa-wa and the plunger thing which he took from Bubber Miley, and he made a classic out of it. He using it with the whole band, but it really started - turned it into something by (unintelligible) Johnny Dunn was the first one. This Johnny Dunn, later on, worked with Mamie Smith and I guess Bessie Smith and Clara Smith and everybody else. But Johnny Dunn, he ended up with Lew Leslie, playing for Florence Mills, you see?
